messages:
sam.sales: FYI ACME asked if we can run a month-long on‑prem POC in their air-gapped DC. They want quantized model bundles, no egress, and a strict upgrade cadence (quarterly at most). Can we do this?

maya.se: short answer: yes, but we need to scope packaging and signing. A few clarifying qs: hardware matrix (GPUs/FP32 vs INT8), how they plan to fetch deltas, and who will hold the root CA.

sam.sales: they gave rough HW: 2 x A10G-equivalent nodes + smaller CPU workers. Preference for INT8 quantized weights to save RAM. No internet; they can accept USB or internal artifact repo sync during maintenance windows.

priya.sec: security checklist: offline bundle signing, SBOM, reproducible build logs, and KMS/HSM integration for keys. Also need to confirm telemetry opt-out and local audit logs.

ben.infra: A10G equiv + INT8 is fine. Quantized bundles (q4/q8) run well. Upside: lower mem, faster packing. Downside: not all ops are exact; need to verify accuracy regressions vs FP32.

maya.se: operationally we offer two packaging flows: 
- delta-bundles (smaller deltas between versions) for regular upgrades
- full-bundles for major changes or emergency hotfixes
We can support USB transfer or scp to an internal repo.

anya.legal: on upgrade cadence: quarterly seems fine contractually, but customers sometimes want monthly security patches. We should offer: quarterly scheduled upgrades + out-of-band emergency security patches (SLA for CVEs). Need to align with pricing.

sam.sales: pricing ask from ACME: is quarterly included in reserved capacity? or extra ops fee per upgrade window?

maya.se: recommend: include 1 scheduled quarterly bundle push in the Dedicated/Private package. Charge a per-window ops fee for extra windows or on-demand full-bundle installs. Keep emergency CVE patches free within SLA X days.

priya.sec: technical blocker: who signs the bundles? We can sign, but customer may insist on dual-sign (Redwood + customer key). We support that but need HSM integration plan. Also anchor timestamping for long-lived air-gapped installs.

ben.infra: implementation note: our build pipeline can emit an SBOM and a signed tarball: 
```
redwood-bundle-v2.3.1.tar.gz
SHA256: <hash>
signature: redwood.sig
sbom.json
```
We can produce delta patches as patches/manifest files. For dual-sign, we can provide a signing hook: customer runs signer locally and we ingest the customer signature into metadata.

deploy-bot: deploy-bundle-check: artifact manifest OK, signature present, sbom present. Manual transfer required for air-gapped endpoints.

maya.se: POC runbook draft: 
1) Preflight: hw validation + network isolation test
2) Baseline eval: run 10k prompts to check regressed outputs against control
3) Iterative tuning: if INT8 causes issues, try q8a or mixed precision
4) Upgrade test: simulate quarterly delta + emergency full-bundle rollback

sam.sales: ACME also asked about rollback windows and rollback SLAs (how quickly can we revert to previous bundle?). They want <2h rollback in worst case.

ben.infra: realistic: for our bundle-based deployment, a rollback (apply previous tar + restart runtime) is typically 20–60 mins if ops team prepared. Two hours is safe if we include pre-staged artifacts and runbook. We'll note prerequisites: pre-staged previous bundle, tested rollback script, and maintenance window.

priya.sec: one more ask: proof of provenance for quantization — provide the quantization seed/version and evaluation artifacts so they can audit quality. Also maintain a signed changelog for each bundle.

anya.legal: I'll draft the upgrade/rollback clause: quarterly scheduled upgrades included; emergency patches within 48h; rollback assistance included for one rollback per upgrade window; additional rollbacks billed.

sam.sales: great. Next steps: maya, can you produce a short POC statement-of-work and runbook we can share with ACME by EOD tomorrow? Include: hardware checklist, transfer methods (USB vs repo), dual-sign options, pricing for extra windows, and rollback SLA language.

maya.se: on it. I'll attach a 2‑page SOW + runbook. Will call out accuracy eval thresholds and test harness for INT8. Expect draft by 18:00 PST tomorrow.

sam.sales: perfect. tagging @priya.sec @anya.legal in case follow-ups pop up. :thumbsup:

priya.sec: cheers. I'll review SOW for security language.

anya.legal: will review pricing and SLA verbiage after SOW lands.

ben.infra: happy to review the runbook and add infra notes.

deploy-bot: reminder: create a tracking ticket for airgap-poc-ACME with checklist and owners.
